knowledge_point.title: Finding the Equation of a Line Perpendicular to a Line Through Two Points

question.:question/worked-solution:
Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other.

First, let's find the slope ${m}_{1}$ of the line passing through the points $(-5,1)$ and $(-6,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{2-1}{-6-(-5)} \\  & =\frac{2-1}{-6+5} \\  & =\frac{1}{-1} \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want a perpendicular line, the slope $m$ of the line we're trying to find must satisfy

$$
m\cdot (-1)=-1\,⇒\,m=1.
$$

We know that the line passes through the point $(0,4).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-4 & =1(x-0) \\ y-4 & =x \\ y & =x + 4\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other.

First, let's find the slope ${m}_{1}$ of the line passing through the points $(2,6)$ and $(5,-6):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{-6-6}{5-2} \\  & =\frac{-6-6}{5-2} \\  & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want a perpendicular line, the slope $m$ of the line we're trying to find must satisfy

$$
m\cdot (-4)=-1\,⇒\,m=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

We know that the line passes through the point $(0,2).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-2 & =\frac{1}{4}(x-0) \\ y-2 & =\frac{x}{4} \\ y & =\frac{x}{4} + 2\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-7 & =\frac{10}{7}(x-0) \\ y-7 & =\frac{10 x}{7} \\ y & =\frac{10 x}{7} + 7\end{aligned}

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Equation of a Line Perpendicular to a Line Through Two Points

question.:question/worked-solution:
Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other.

First, let's find the slope ${m}_{1}$ of the line passing through the points $(8,8)$ and $(-8,-8):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{-8-8}{-8-8} \\  & =\frac{-8-8}{-8-8} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want a perpendicular line, the slope $m$ of the line we're trying to find must satisfy

$$
m\cdot (1)=-1\,⇒\,m=-1.
$$

We know that the line passes through the point $(0,0).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-0 & =-1(x-0) \\ y & =-x \\ y & =-x\end{aligned}
$$
